Cauchy (mutual) convergence is a useful result when you have to prove
convergence but do not have a good candidate for a limit. Cauchy convergence
requires only information on pairs $(x_{n},x_{m})$.

:::{.definition data-title="Cauchy Convergence"}

A real sequence $\{  x_{n} \}$ converges if and only if it is Cauchy, that is $$\forall \epsilon >0, \exists N=N_{\epsilon}~s.t.~|x_{n}-x_{m}|>\epsilon ,\forall n,m>N,$$or in other words $x_{n}-x_{m}\to 0$ as $n,m \to \infty$ independently.

:::
